turns.text: Behind the technical name Lasso, what intuitive problem were researchers confronting?
As datasets grew wider, analysts needed models that could avoid overfitting and identify useful variables. Ridge regression shrank coefficients, but it did not usually set them to zero.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?
The lasso adds an L1 penalty to regression. The geometry of that penalty naturally creates exact zeros, so prediction and selection are tied together.
Why did the idea outlive one paper or experiment? What did later researchers actually inherit?

Experts generally treat Lasso as a standard tool for sparse, interpretable linear modeling. Its long-term legacy is regularization-driven feature selection, especially in high-dimensional statistics, genomics, and transparent predictive modeling.
Lasso mattered not only as a result, but as a method that later researchers could test, adapt, and extend.
